articles.title: The India Company Compliance Checklist I Wish I Had in Week One
articles.excerpt: When I set up my first company in India, I assumed incorporation was the hard part. It was not. The real work started after the certificate arrived, when a steady list of compliance tasks began landin…
articles.body: When I set up my first company in India, I assumed incorporation was the hard part. It was not. The real work started after the certificate arrived, when a steady list of compliance tasks began landing on my desk. Here is the short checklist I wish I had kept from week one. Right after incorporation Open the current account early. Banks ask for several documents and the process can take longer than you expect. Get your PAN and TAN sorted and saved in one shared folder that your cofounder and accountant can both reach. Check whether GST registration applies to you now or later. Registering too early can mean filing returns with nothing to report, which is still work. The recurring stuff Board meetings and minutes. Even a tiny private limited company needs them on a regular schedule.

articles.title: Agents Now Plan Tasks Across Your Codebase
articles.excerpt: The throughline this week is agents moving from single-shot completions to multi-step execution with real consequences—writing PRs, merging changesets, routing tickets without a human in the loop. Wha…
articles.body: The throughline this week is agents moving from single-shot completions to multi-step execution with real consequences—writing PRs, merging changesets, routing tickets without a human in the loop. What's shifting isn't the capability ceiling; it's where the orchestration layer lives. Tools that used to hand you a diff now hand you a merged PR. Raycast AI adds agentic planning with task automation Raycast's AI Chat can now run multi-step tasks autonomously—chaining extension calls, executing code, retrying on failure—without per-request interruptions. Billing moves from rate limits to usage-based, and bring-your-own-subscription support (Claude, ChatGPT) means you can route through existing credits.

articles.title: SOC 2: Understanding the Assurance Standard for Service Organizations
articles.excerpt: As SaaS platforms, cloud services, fintech applications, and other digital services become increasingly connected to customer data, organizations are facing greater expectations around how they protec…
articles.body: As SaaS platforms, cloud services, fintech applications, and other digital services become increasingly connected to customer data, organizations are facing greater expectations around how they protect and manage that information. Customers and enterprise buyers often want more than a security statement—they want credible evidence that relevant controls have been independently evaluated. This is where SOC 2 has become particularly relevant for service organizations. SOC 2 is an attestation framework developed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). It focuses on evaluating controls related to areas such as security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy, depending on the criteria selected for the engagement.

articles.title: Auth for Laravel — headless multi-guard login with 2FA, passkeys and JWT sessions
articles.excerpt: Every API-backed Laravel app we built needed sign-in, and the hand-written version kept having the same small gaps: a login error that told you whether an email was registered, a password reset that l…
articles.body: Every API-backed Laravel app we built needed sign-in, and the hand-written version kept having the same small gaps: a login error that told you whether an email was registered, a password reset that left old sessions alive, a two-factor step a client could skip. Each one is minor. Together they are how accounts get taken over. So we pulled all of it into one package and open-sourced it. What it does Auth for Laravel is headless account authentication for Laravel apps behind a mobile app or a single-page frontend. It owns the policy and orchestration; your app keeps its screens. Four ways to sign in : password, magic link, email code and passkey. A challenge engine for the second step (authenticator code, backup code or passkey), including forced enrolment when a guard requires two-factor.

articles.body: For a couple of weeks I couldn't decide how to build my card game app: pick a ready-made engine, or write my own code. On one side were real game engines: Unity, Godot, the usual suspects. On the other was the slightly crazy option of writing it myself in TypeScript on top of React Native. This post is about why I ended up with the crazy option, what it gave me, and what it cost. The app is called Decks. It's on iOS now with fourteen games: nine solitaires (Klondike, Yukon, Spider, FreeCell, Pyramid, TriPeaks, Golf, Black Hole, Spanish Solitaire) and five puzzles (Codebreak, Triples, Memo, Tower of Hanoi and a two-tower variant). articles.body: TL;DR Some Pixel owners reported worse performance after installing September’s Android 17 QPR1 update. GrapheneOS says it has found a regression in the update that can cause lag, stuttering, freezes, and app crashes under memory pressure. While GrapheneOS has already patched the problem, stock Pixel users are still waiting for Google to release a fix. Android 17 QPR1 was supposed to improve Pixel phones, but for a noticeable number of owners, the September update seems to have had the opposite effect. We recently asked Android Authority readers how their Pixels were behaving after installing the update , and performance problems stood out as the most common complaint among those who reported new issues. articles.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
articles.excerpt: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he…
articles.body: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.” “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype , steered by zealots, inescapable. The CEO of Springboards and I are far from alone. Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now. On the one hand, public feelings are souring fast.
